# Isleta 2.1.1
Volume and brightness now appear in the notch instead of in Apple's HUD, without your having to turn it on first. Isleta needs Accessibility for that, which it asks for on the first run.
## New
- **Isleta is open source, under the MIT License.** The whole app is on GitHub — the same signed and notarized build you are updating to, with everything behind it now public.
## Improved
- **Isleta replaces the volume and brightness HUDs by default.** Press a volume or brightness key and the level appears in the notch rather than in the middle of your screen. It needs Accessibility, which the first run asks for, and two switches in Settings put Apple's HUDs back. - **The lock screen's notch taps under your pointer.** Move onto it and the padlock widens with the same small trackpad tap the island gives you when the Mac is unlocked. Nothing else on that screen taps. - **A day that is over says so.** The day view now says "No more events today" once the day's events have finished, and keeps "No events today" for a day that never had any.
## Fixed
- **"Lossless" and "Dolby Atmos" no longer linger after the music stops.** The badge belongs to the track it describes, so nothing is shown under "Not playing".
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is on by default, and it needs Accessibility.** Two switches in Settings hand the keys back. Quitting Isleta hands them back too; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels. - **Today and tomorrow show five entries and then a count.** A busy pair of days says how many it could not fit rather than scrolling.

# Isleta 2.1.0
The island now says what your power just did — "Charging" or "On Battery" beside the battery, the same way it names the key you pressed for volume and brightness.
## New
- **Plugging in and unplugging say so in words.** The island widens beside the notch and shows "Charging" or "On Battery" next to the battery glyph, with the level beside it, then goes away on its own. A battery symbol with a small bolt in it and one without are hard to tell apart in a notch; the word is not. - **The same for the other power moments.** "Charged", "Low Battery", and "Low Power On" or "Low Power Off" when macOS switches the mode.
## Improved
- **Power keeps the readable half of the island when music is playing.** The word sits where the album cover would go and the track's own sliver moves to the other side, rather than the charger showing up as a bar with nothing to say what it measures.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is off until you turn it on, and it needs Accessibility.** Quitting Isleta hands your keys straight back; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. # Isleta 2.0.1
Turning a page is smoother, the day view holds its size, and a day with nothing on it now says so instead of looking empty by accident.
## Improved
- **Turning a page is smoother.** The three pages no longer redraw themselves on every frame of the swipe, so a day full of events or a playing track no longer makes the carousel stutter on its way past.
## Fixed
- **The day view's bottom edge stopped jumping up.** Opening today and tomorrow from the date, then changing track — or anything else arriving on the island — pulled the bottom edge up and cut the last row off. It now stays where it opened, whatever else happens. - **A day with no events says so.** "No events today" and "No events tomorrow", each in its own place, instead of a column that simply started at Tomorrow or stopped early. A free day and a day whose events failed to load looked identical before this.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
